deal_math.parity_note: 1:1 market-cap parity works out to about $496 per TSLA at current prices (+29%), which clears the $450 floor.
deal_math.collar_note: An all-stock deal at a fixed ratio leaves Tesla holders exposed if SPCX falls before the vote. To win an independent Tesla vote it likely needs downside protection (a collar or price floor). SpaceX holders would resist, because it shifts value to Tesla holders if SPCX drops. This is general M&A practice, not deal-specific.
deal_math.reverse_note: Reverse case: Tesla acquires SpaceX. Tesla has one class of stock, so Musk's dual-class control would end. Shown for completeness; low probability.

fcc.note: The SpaceX-Grain transfer applications were filed Oct 9 (ULS 0012212612 lead) and ask for expedited consent. On Nov 10, 2026 the FCC Wireless Bureau accepted them for filing in WT Docket 26-313 (Public Notice DA 26-1218): petitions/comments due Dec 1, oppositions Dec 8, so a grant is unlikely before mid-December. The earlier T-Mobile to Grain proceeding was WT 25-178. The FCC's informal goal is 180 days for transaction review (general practice).

why: On SpaceX's Oct 20 earnings call, Musk said the Tesla and SpaceX boards have each formed a special committee of independent directors to look at a merger. He called it a good idea but said no terms are agreed and there's no guarantee.

Tesla's DEF 14A (Oct 19) still set a routine Dec 3 meeting with no merger item, so any deal goes the normal route: committee talks, fairness opinions, an S-4, then a separate announcement and a special meeting, most likely in 2027. Tesla needs 50% of all outstanding shares to approve.
With committees confirmed and Bloomberg reporting (Nov 12) that talks are progressing, the rules model puts a merger letter or agreement by Jun 30, 2027 at 63%. That is a judgment call, not data.

Prediction markets price it at 73% on the liquidity-weighted Kalshi and Polymarket composite. Markets often move before the news hits the wire, so they get 48% of the weight, more when trading is heavy and less when it is thin. Dashboard number: 52% x 62.6% + 48% x 73.0% = 67.6%.

Catalysts to watch: Starship Flight 15 (NET Nov 20), the Nov 20 and Dec 18 monthly options expirations, the Dec 3 annual meeting Q&A, the Dec 8 SpaceX unlock, and any banker or law-firm hire by the committees. Unlock days and Starship launch days are less likely days for a deal letter.

kill.why: If a routine meeting is set with no SpaceX language, the 2026-meeting merger path is closed. Letter odds by mid-2027 are modeled as 0.6 x the pre-kill merger share: a clean routine proxy is evidence against a live deal, but a 2027 special meeting is still possible. This is judgment, not data. For comparison, Polymarket's Jun 30, 2027 contract is shown in details.

starship._why: NET Nov 8 comes from planning-grade sources: the CADENA air-traffic planning slides of Oct 8 (cited by Wikipedia), and NASASpaceflight reporting on Oct 10 plus Musk's '4-6 weeks' remark (per thelaunchwindow). After a failure, days +1 to +5 get x0.2. The status comes from data/events_state.json (set by watch.py or by hand) or from this config.

docs._doc: Used once the state is meeting_only (Dec 3 AGM set, routine). Headline = merger letter (or definitive agreement) by `by`, conditional on none so far. Dashboard number = (1 - market_weight) x rules model + market_weight x market composite, plus any smart-money nudge.
docs._rules_why: Rules model: 0.6 x the pre-proxy merger share (letter_after_kill). With the committee signal on (Oct 20: both boards formed special committees), that share is 94%, so the rules number is 0.6 x 0.94 = 56%. The 0.6 keeps a haircut because Musk said no terms are agreed, there's no guarantee, and the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares. Judgment, not data. Nov 12, 2026: raised from 0.5637 to 0.60 after Bloomberg ('people familiar') reported talks are progressing with boards and advisers working through terms and governance; open hurdles (Tesla China, SpaceX defense ties, shareholder/regulatory approval) keep the haircut. Judgment, not data. Nov 15, 2026 calibration review: raised from 0.60 to 0.64. The Nov 12 step (0.5637 to 0.60) was an under-reaction: a Bloomberg 'people familiar' report that talks are progressing and advisers are working through terms is worth roughly a 1.4x odds update, which gives ~0.64. Part of the old haircut was also completion risk (the 50%-of-shares vote, Texas/China/defense reviews), which matters for closing, not for announcing. The remaining haircut covers failure to agree terms and slippage past Jun 30, 2027. Judgment, not data.
docs._month_why: How the rules model spreads the letter odds over time. Spread fairly evenly, with a bit more weight in Dec (AGM Q&A, Day-180 unlock) and Feb (after SpaceX's Q4 results). Then multiplied by catalyst-day weights below. Oct 22, 2026: shifted 11 pts of weight from Oct-Dec 2026 into Jan-Jun 2027 after Bloomberg ('people familiar') said an announcement is targeted for the first half of 2027 and Reuters (person with direct knowledge) said Musk's public comments could delay the process by several weeks and talks are at an early stage. Total letter odds by Jun 30, 2027 unchanged; judgment, not data. Nov 12, 2026: shifted 6 pts of weight back into Dec 2026 (from Mar-Jun 2027) after Bloomberg ('people familiar', 3:09 PM ET) said merger talks are progressing, advisers are discussing terms, and a deal could be announced as soon as December but could slip into 2027. Judgment, not data. Nov 15, 2026 calibration review: Jan 2027 raised from 14% to 17% (1 pt each from Feb, Mar, Apr). With December as the 'as soon as' case, January is the first slip month and Tesla's Q4 report lands late January, so it should not sit below December. The rules model keeps December as the early scenario (about 22% of its Jun 30 odds land by Dec 31, vs about 37% in the markets): no merger item at the Dec 3 AGM, fairness opinions still to come, and the holidays. Inside December, odds are shifted toward Dec 7-23 (AGM day weight cut from 4x to 2x, Dec 8 unlock 0.4x, holiday lull 0.5x). The Dec 18 options expiry gets no weight: nothing ties a deal to it.
docs._market_why: Share of the dashboard number taken from the prediction-market composite. Since Nov 15, 2026 it scales with market depth: weight = 30% + 30% x L / (L + $10K), where L is the median over the last 3 days of total 24h volume across live contracts. Thin weeks (~$5K/day) get about 40% (the old fixed weight), busy weeks ($20K+/day) about 50%, capped at 60% so the rules model always keeps at least 40%.
docs.market: Composite: every live Kalshi (definitive agreement before X) and Polymarket (announced by X) contract counts as the same event. Since Nov 15, 2026: (1) each contract's weight is its liquidity quality: 24h volume (saturating, half at $500) x spread tightness (full at 2c or less; a last-trade quote counts 25%); (2) a move one contract makes on its own is damped instead of dropped: compared with the median of its own quotes over the past 24h, it keeps the share of the move other contracts confirm, plus up to half the rest (less when the book is thin), so a lone spike counts partly and a market-wide move counts nearly in full; (3) expired contracts and quotes more than 12h old (or 3h behind the other contracts) are left out; (4) a liquidity-weighted monotone fit is drawn through the rest. Polymarket 'announced' can include a non-binding letter while Kalshi needs a definitive agreement, so Kalshi should trade at or below Polymarket for the same date; in practice it trades at or above, so no venue adjustment is applied.
docs.smart_money: Flag 'Market moved before news': a contract moves 5+ pts in 24h with at least $1K traded and no filing or strict-filtered deal headline in that window. Nudge: if a flagged-quality move is 10+ pts within 72h, the dashboard adds 25% of that move (capped at 4 pts) on top of the blend, until news explains it or the move ages out.
